questions.question: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which diagonal BD = 70 cm. AL ⊥ BD and CM ⊥ BD such that AL = 18 cm and CM = 20. Find the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral ABCD.
questions.questionHtml: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which diagonal BD = 70 cm. AL ⊥ BD and CM ⊥ BD such that AL = 18 cm and CM = 20. Find the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral ABCD.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The area of a general quadrilateral equals half the product of its diagonal and the sum of perpendiculars dropped on it.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × Diagonal × (Sum of perpendiculars)

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 70 × (18 + 20)

⇒ Area = 35 × 38 = 1330

∴ The correct answer is 1330 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diagonal BD = 70 cm

Perpendicular AL = 18 cm

Perpendicular CM = 20 cm

Formula Used:

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height

Area of Quadrilateral ABCD = Area of ΔABD + Area of ΔBCD

Calculation:

⇒ Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × BD × AL

⇒ Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × 70 × 18 = 630 cm2

⇒ Area of ΔBCD = 1/2 × BD × CM

⇒ Area of ΔBCD = 1/2 × 70 × 20 = 700 cm2

⇒ Total Area = 630 + 700 = 1330 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 1330 cm2.

Additional Information

Area of Rhombus

The area is calculated as half the product of its diagonals: Area = 1/2 × d1 × d2.

Area of Trapezium

Calculated as half the sum of parallel sides multiplied by the distance between them: Area = 1/2 × (a + b) × h.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose vertices all lie on a single circle. Its area can be found using Brahmagupta's formula: Area = √((s−a)(s−b)(s−c)(s−d)), where s is the semi-perimeter.

questions.question: A tank when full can be emptied by an outlet pipe A in 5.6 hours, while an inlet pipe B can fill the same empty tank in 7 hours. If pipes A and B are turned on alternatively for 1 hour each starting with pipe A when the tank is full, how long will it take to empty the tank?
questions.questionHtml: A tank when full can be emptied by an outlet pipe A in 5.6 hours, while an inlet pipe B can fill the same empty tank in 7 hours. If pipes A and B are turned on alternatively for 1 hour each starting with pipe A when the tank is full, how long will it take to empty the tank?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total capacity = LCM(5.6, 7) = 28 units.

Efficiency: Pipe A = +5 units/hr (emptying), Pipe B = −4 units/hr (filling).

Net work in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 5 − 4 = 1 unit emptied.

Safe zone before Pipe A's final turn = 28 − 5 = 23 units.

Time for 23 units = 23 × 2 = 46 hours, remaining 5 units emptied by A in 1 hour.

∴ The correct answer is 47 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by outlet pipe A to empty the tank = 5.6 hours.

Time taken by inlet pipe B to fill the tank = 7 hours.

Pipes are opened alternatively for 1 hour each, starting with A.

Calculations:

Pipe Hours Total Work Efficiency
Pipe A 5.6 28 5
Pipe B 7 −4

⇒ Let emptying the tank be positive work (+), and filling be negative work (−).

⇒ Work done in the 1st hour by A = 5 units.

⇒ Work done in the 2nd hour by B = −4 units.

⇒ Total work done in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

⇒ Since A can empty 5 units in its turn, we calculate full cycles for 28 − 5 = 23 units.

⇒ Time required to empty 23 units = 23 cycles × 2 hours/cycle = 46 hours.

⇒ Remaining work = 28 − 23 = 5 units.

⇒ In the 47th hour, Pipe A will empty the remaining 5 units in exactly 1 hour.

⇒ Total time taken = 46 + 1 = 47 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 47 hours.

Additional Information

Pipes and Cisterns

Inlet pipes add to the volume (+ efficiency) and outlet pipes remove volume (− efficiency). The total work is assumed as the LCM of the given time periods.

Alternate Work Concept

When positive and negative work happen alternatively, always subtract the positive work of the final step from the total work to avoid overcounting cycles, similar to the monkey climbing a greased pole puzzle.

Efficiency vs Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

questions.question: If a : b = 2 : 3, b : c = 5 : 7, then find the ratio c : a.
questions.questionHtml: If a : b = 2 : 3, b : c  = 5 : 7, then find the ratio c : a.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To find the ratio of the extremes (c : a) directly, multiply the given ratios and invert.

⇒ a / c = (a / b) × (b / c)

⇒ a / c = (2 / 3) × (5 / 7) = 10 / 21

⇒ c / a = 21 / 10

∴ The correct answer is 21 : 10.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ a : b = 2 : 3

⇒ b : c = 5 : 7

Calculations:

⇒ To combine the ratios, make the common term 'b' equal in both.

⇒ The value of b is 3 in the first ratio and 5 in the second.

⇒ Multiply the first ratio by 5 and the second ratio by 3 (LCM of 3 and 5 is 15).

⇒ a : b = (2 × 5) : (3 × 5) = 10 : 15

⇒ b : c = (5 × 3) : (7 × 3) = 15 : 21

⇒ Combining them, we get a : b : c = 10 : 15 : 21

⇒ Therefore, the ratio c : a = 21 : 10

∴ The correct answer is 21 : 10.

Additional Information

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, the result is called a compound ratio. For a : b and c : d, it is ac : bd.

Duplicate and Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a2 : b2. The sub-duplicate ratio of a : b is √a : √b.

Invertendo and Alternendo

For a proportion a : b = c : d, invertendo gives b : a = d : c, and alternendo gives a : c = b : d.

questions.question: In a circle centered at O, a diameter AB is extended to a point C outside the circle. CD is a tangent at point D on the circle. If CD = 7√3 cm and ∠DBC = 120°, then the length of the diameter of the circle is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle centered at O, a diameter AB is extended to a point C outside the circle. CD is a tangent at point D on the circle. If CD = 7√3 cm and ∠DBC = 120°, then the length of the diameter of the circle is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since ABC forms a straight line, ∠OBD = 180° − 120° = 60°.

Because OB and OD are radii, ΔOBD is equilateral, making ∠BOD = 60°.

The tangent CD is perpendicular to radius OD, so ∠ODC = 90°.

In right-angled ΔODC, tan(60°) = CD ÷ OD ⇒ √3 = 7√3 ÷ R.

Solving this gives R = 7 cm. The diameter is 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ CD is tangent to the circle at point D.

⇒ CD = 7√3 cm

⇒ ∠DBC = 120°

Formula Used:

⇒ In a right-angled triangle, tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base

⇒ Angles forming a linear pair add up to 180°

Calculations:

⇒ Since point B lies on the straight line AC, ∠OBD and ∠DBC form a linear pair.

⇒ ∠OBD + ∠DBC = 180°

⇒ ∠OBD = 180° − 120° = 60°

⇒ In ΔOBD, OB and OD are both radii of the same circle, so OB = OD.

⇒ Angles opposite to equal sides are equal, hence ∠ODB = ∠OBD = 60°.

⇒ Using the sum of angles in a triangle, ∠BOD = 180° − (60° + 60°) = 60°.

⇒ Because CD is a tangent at D, the radius OD is perpendicular to it. Therefore, ∠ODC = 90°.

⇒ In right-angled ΔODC, ∠DOC = 60°.

⇒ tan(∠DOC) = CD ÷ OD

⇒ tan(60°) = 7√3 ÷ R

⇒ √3 = 7√3 ÷ R

⇒ R = 7 cm

⇒ The diameter of the circle = 2 × R = 2 × 7 = 14 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.

Additional Information

Tangent-Radius Theorem

A tangent to a circle always forms a right angle (90°) with the radius drawn to the exact point of tangency. This geometric property is universally useful for creating right-angled triangles to solve for missing lengths.

Isosceles Triangle Property

When two sides of a triangle are equal (such as the radii of a circle drawn from the center), the angles strictly opposite to those sides must also be equal. This frequently helps deduce that a triangle is equilateral.

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its two interior opposite angles. In ΔOBD, ∠DBC acts as an exterior angle, ensuring that ∠DBC = ∠BOD + ∠ODB (120° = 60° + 60°).

questions.question: If x = 4 + √6 and y = 4 - √6 then the value of x 2 + y 2 is:
questions.questionHtml: If x = 4 + √6 and y = 4 - √6 then the value of x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct algebraic identity: (a + b)2 + (a − b)2 = 2(a2 + b2)

Here, the given values are x = 4 + √6 and y = 4 − √6.

Substituting a = 4 and b = √6 into the identity directly:

⇒ x2 + y2 = 2 × (42 + (√6)2)

⇒ x2 + y2 = 2 × (16 + 6) = 2 × 22 = 44

∴ The correct answer is 44.

Alternate Method

Given:

x = 4 + √6 and y = 4 − √6

Formula Used:

x2 + y2 = (x + y)2 − 2xy

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of x and y (x + y) = (4 + √6) + (4 − √6) = 8

⇒ Product of x and y (xy) = (4 + √6) × (4 − √6)

⇒ Using (a + b)(a − b) = a2 − b2

⇒ xy = 42 − (√6)2 = 16 − 6 = 10

⇒ Now substituting these values into the formula:

⇒ x2 + y2 = (8)2 − 2 × 10

⇒ x2 + y2 = 64 − 20 = 44

∴ The correct answer is 44.

Additional Information

Difference of Squares

The formula a2 − b2 = (a + b)(a − b) is very useful for multiplying conjugate expressions directly without expanding.

Conjugate Surds

Expressions of the form a + √b and a − √b are known as conjugate surds. Their sum and product always result in rational numbers.

Subtraction of Perfect Squares

(a + b)2 − (a − b)2 = 4ab. This identity helps directly compute the difference between squares of conjugates.

Sum of Cubes Identity

x3 + y3 = (x + y)(x2 − xy + y2) or equivalently (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y).

questions.question: If \(\rm \cos27°=\frac{P}{q}\) , then find the value of cosec 27° - cos 63°.
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm \cos27°=\frac{P}{q}\), then find the value of cosec 27° - cos 63°.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Convert to the same angle using complementary property: cos 63° = sin(90° − 27°) = sin 27°.

Simplify expression: cosec 27° − sin 27° = (1 − sin2 27°) / sin 27° = cos2 27° / sin 27°.

From given cos 27° = p / q, we find sin 27° = √(1 − p2/q2) = √(q2 − p2) / q.

Substitute these values directly: (p / q)2 ÷ [√(q2 − p2) / q] = p2 / [q√(q2 − p2)].

∴ The correct answer is p2 / (q√(q2 − p2)).

Alternate Method

Given:

cos 27° = p / q

Concept Used:

In a right-angled triangle, cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

By Pythagoras Theorem: Perpendicular = √(Hypotenuse2 − Base2)

cos(90° − θ) = sin θ

cosec θ = Hypotenuse / Perpendicular

Calculations:

⇒ Base = p, Hypotenuse = q

⇒ Perpendicular = √(q2 − p2)

⇒ We need to find the value of: cosec 27° − cos 63°

⇒ Using complementary angle relation, cos 63° = cos(90° − 27°) = sin 27°

⇒ sin 27° = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse = √(q2 − p2) / q

⇒ cosec 27° = Hypotenuse / Perpendicular = q / √(q2 − p2)

⇒ Expression = [q / √(q2 − p2)] − [√(q2 − p2) / q]

⇒ Expression = [q2 − (q2 − p2)] / [q√(q2 − p2)]

⇒ Expression = [q2 − q2 + p2] / [q√(q2 − p2)]

⇒ Expression = p2 / [q√(q2 − p2)]

∴ The correct answer is p2 / (q√(q2 − p2)).

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1 and cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ.

Complementary Angles

The trigonometric ratios of complementary angles are related as sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the base and the perpendicular: H2 = B2 + P2.

questions.question: The average of first 92 even numbers is
questions.questionHtml: The average of first 92 even numbers is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The average of the first n even numbers can be directly determined using the formula: (n + 1).

Here, the number of even numbers (n) = 92.

⇒ Average = 92 + 1 = 93

∴ The correct answer is 93.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total number of terms (n) = 92

The series represents the first 92 even numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8, ..., 184

Formula Used:

For any uniformly spaced series (Arithmetic Progression), Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2

Calculations:

⇒ First term of the series (a) = 2

⇒ Last term of the series (l) = 92 × 2 = 184

⇒ Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = (2 + 184) ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 186 ÷ 2 = 93

∴ The correct answer is 93.

Additional Information

Average of first n Odd Numbers

The average of the first n odd numbers is always equal to n.

Average of first n Natural Numbers

The average of the first n natural numbers is evaluated as (n + 1) ÷ 2.

Average of Uniformly Spaced Numbers

For any consecutive series or Arithmetic Progression, the average is exactly midway between the limits: Average = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

questions.question: Simplify (5z - 7y) 2 + (7z + 5y) 2 - 49z 2
questions.questionHtml: Simplify (5z - 7y)<sup>2</sup> + (7z + 5y)<sup>2</sup> - 49z<sup>2</sup>
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the Brahmagupta−Fibonacci algebraic identity: (ax − by)2 + (bx + ay)2 = (a2 + b2)(x2 + y2)

For the given expression (5z − 7y)2 + (7z + 5y)2, substitute a = 5, b = 7, x = z, and y = y.

Sum = (52 + 72)(z2 + y2) = (25 + 49)(z2 + y2) = 74(z2 + y2)

Expression becomes: 74z2 + 74y2 − 49z2

Result = 25z2 + 74y2

∴ The correct answer is 25z2 + 74y2.

Alternate Method

Given:

(5z − 7y)2 + (7z + 5y)2 − 49z2

Formula Used:

(a − b)2 = a2 − 2ab + b2

(a + b)2 = a2 + 2ab + b2

Calculations:

⇒ Expanding the first term: (5z − 7y)2 = (5z)2 − 2 × (5z) × (7y) + (7y)2 = 25z2 − 70zy + 49y2

⇒ Expanding the second term: (7z + 5y)2 = (7z)2 + 2 × (7z) × (5y) + (5y)2 = 49z2 + 70zy + 25y2

⇒ Adding both expansions: (25z2 − 70zy + 49y2) + (49z2 + 70zy + 25y2)

⇒ Grouping similar terms: (25z2 + 49z2) + (−70zy + 70zy) + (49y2 + 25y2)

⇒ The middle terms cancel out: 74z2 + 0 + 74y2

⇒ Now, subtract the remaining 49z2 from the original expression: 74z2 + 74y2 − 49z2

⇒ Final simplification: (74 − 49)z2 + 74y2 = 25z2 + 74y2

∴ The correct answer is 25z2 + 74y2.

Additional Information

Brahmagupta−Fibonacci Identity

This identity expresses the product of two sums of squares as a sum of squares: (a2 + b2)(x2 + y2) = (ax − by)2 + (bx + ay)2. It is incredibly useful for instantly expanding and grouping complex crossed algebraic pairs without calculating individual terms.

Standard Algebraic Identities

Other essential identities for quick simplification include: (a + b)2 + (a − b)2 = 2(a2 + b2) and (a + b)2 − (a − b)2 = 4ab.

BODMAS Rule in Algebra

Always follow the order of operations when simplifying polynomials: evaluate brackets and exponent powers first, then handle the addition or subtraction of grouped coefficients.

questions.question: Let PQR be a right angled triangle, right-angled at R. Let PQ = 29 cm, QR = 21 cm and ∠Q = θ. Find the value of cos 2 θ – sin 2 θ.
questions.questionHtml: Let PQR be a right angled triangle, right-angled at R. Let PQ = 29 cm, QR = 21 cm and ∠Q = θ. Find the value of cos<sup>2</sup> θ – sin<sup>2</sup> θ.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In a right-angled triangle, if the hypotenuse is 29 and the base is 21, the third side directly forms the standard Pythagorean triplet (20, 21, 29).

Thus, Perpendicular = 20.

cos θ = 21/29 and sin θ = 20/29

cos2 θ − sin2 θ = (21/29)2 − (20/29)2 = (441 − 400) / 841 = 41/841

∴ The correct answer is 41/841.

Alternate Method

Given:

In right-angled triangle PQR, right-angled at R:

Hypotenuse (PQ) = 29 cm

Base (QR) = 21 cm

∠Q = θ

Formula Used:

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse2 = Perpendicular2 + Base2

cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

Calculation:

⇒ PQ2 = PR2 + QR2

⇒ 292 = PR2 + 212

⇒ 841 = PR2 + 441

⇒ PR2 = 841 − 441 = 400

⇒ PR = √400 = 20 cm

⇒ cos θ = QR / PQ = 21/29

⇒ sin θ = PR / PQ = 20/29

Now, substitute the values into the required expression:

⇒ cos2 θ − sin2 θ = (21/29)2 − (20/29)2

⇒ cos2 θ − sin2 θ = (441/841) − (400/841)

⇒ cos2 θ − sin2 θ = (441 − 400) / 841 = 41/841

∴ The correct answer is 41/841.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers a, b, and c that satisfy the equation a2 + b2 = c2. Commonly asked triplets in exams include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (20, 21, 29).

Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental identities are: sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1, 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ, and 1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ.

Double Angle Formula

The term evaluated in the question, cos2 θ − sin2 θ, is mathematically equivalent to the double angle formula cos(2θ).

questions.question: Which number among 38211, 38121, 32118, and 31128 is divisible by 24?
questions.questionHtml: Which number among 38211, 38121, 32118, and 31128 is divisible by 24?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by 24, it must be divisible by both 3 and 8.

Since 8 is an even number, any number divisible by it must also be even, eliminating 38211 and 38121.

Check the last 3 digits of the remaining numbers for divisibility by 8.

For 32118: 118 ÷ 8 = 14.75 → Not divisible.

For 31128: 128 ÷ 8 = 16 → Completely divisible.

∴ The correct answer is 31128.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numbers to check: 38211, 38121, 32118, 31128

Concept Used:

Divisibility rule of 24: A number is divisible by 24 if it is divisible by its co-prime factors, 3 and 8.

Calculations:

⇒ Step 1: Check divisibility by 3 (sum of the digits must be a multiple of 3).

⇒ Sum of digits for all options = 3 + 8 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 15.

⇒ Since 15 is divisible by 3, all given numbers are divisible by 3.

⇒ Step 2: Check divisibility by 8 (last three digits must form a number divisible by 8).

⇒ 38211 → The last digit is odd, so it is not divisible by 8.

⇒ 38121 → The last digit is odd, so it is not divisible by 8.

⇒ 32118 → The last three digits are 118. 118 ÷ 8 = 14.75 → Not divisible.

⇒ 31128 → The last three digits are 128. 128 ÷ 8 = 16 → Divisible.

⇒ Thus, 31128 is the only number divisible by both 3 and 8.

∴ The correct answer is 31128.

Additional Information

Divisibility by Composite Numbers

To check divisibility by a composite number, test the divisibility of its co-prime factors. For example, since 24 = 3 × 8 (where 3 and 8 are co-prime), a number divisible by 24 must be divisible by both 3 and 8.

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is a multiple of 8.

questions.question: P and Q take part in 400 m race. P runs at 12 km/hr. P gives Q a start of 20 m and still beats him by 13 seconds. The speed of Q is: (Round up to two decimal places.)
questions.questionHtml: P and Q take part in 400 m race. P runs at 12 km/hr. P gives Q a start of 20 m and still beats him by 13 seconds. The speed of Q is: (Round up to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed of P in m/s = 12 × (5/18) = 10/3 m/s.

Time taken by P to finish the race = 400 ÷ (10/3) = 120 seconds.

Time taken by Q = 120 + 13 = 133 seconds.

Distance run by Q = 400 − 20 = 380 m.

Speed of Q = 380 ÷ 133 = 20/7 m/s ⇒ (20/7) × (18/5) = 72/7 = 10.29 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 10.29 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance of race = 400 m

Speed of P = 12 km/hr

Start distance given to Q = 20 m

Time by which P beats Q = 13 seconds

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed conversion: 1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s

Calculations:

⇒ Speed of P = 12 × (5/18) = 10/3 m/s

⇒ Time taken by P to complete the race = 400 ÷ (10/3) = 120 seconds

⇒ P gives Q a start of 20 m, so distance covered by Q = 400 − 20 = 380 m

⇒ P beats Q by 13 seconds, so Time taken by Q = Time taken by P + 13

⇒ Time taken by Q = 120 + 13 = 133 seconds

⇒ Speed of Q in m/s = Distance ÷ Time = 380 ÷ 133 = 20/7 m/s

⇒ Speed of Q in km/hr = (20/7) × (18/5) = 72/7 km/hr

⇒ Speed of Q ≈ 10.2857 km/hr

⇒ Rounding up to two decimal places, Speed of Q = 10.29 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 10.29 km/hr.

Additional Information

Start Distance in Races

If A gives B a start of x meters in a race of L meters, it means A has to run the complete L meters while B only has to run (L − x) meters.

Start Time in Races

If A beats B by t seconds, it implies B takes t seconds more than A to complete his designated track distance.

Speed Conversions

To convert km/hr into m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s into km/hr, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.question: If \(\rm \sin A=\frac{5}{13}\) , then find the value of \(\rm \frac{\cos A-2\tan A}{\sin A+3\tan A}\) .
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm \sin A=\frac{5}{13}\), then find the value of \(\rm \frac{\cos A-2\tan A}{\sin A+3\tan A}\).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Using the 5-12-13 triplet for sin A = 5/13, we get P = 5, H = 13, and B = 12.

Thus, cos A = 12/13 and tan A = 5/12.

Numerator = 12/13 − 2×(5/12) = (144 − 130) / 156 = 14/156.

Denominator = 5/13 + 3×(5/12) = (60 + 195) / 156 = 255/156.

Value = Numerator ÷ Denominator = 14/255.

∴ The correct answer is 14/255.

Alternate Method

Given:

sin A = 5/13

Formula Used:

In a right-angled triangle:

sin A = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

cos A = Base ÷ Hypotenuse

tan A = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Pythagoras Theorem: (Hypotenuse)2 = (Perpendicular)2 + (Base)2

Calculations:

⇒ Let Perpendicular = 5 and Hypotenuse = 13

⇒ Base = √(132 − 52) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12

⇒ cos A = 12/13

⇒ tan A = 5/12

⇒ Numerator = cos A − 2×tan A = 12/13 − 2×(5/12) = 12/13 − 10/12

⇒ Numerator = (144 − 130) / 156 = 14/156

⇒ Denominator = sin A + 3×tan A = 5/13 + 3×(5/12) = 5/13 + 15/12

⇒ Denominator = (60 + 195) / 156 = 255/156

⇒ Required Value = (14/156) ÷ (255/156) = 14/255

∴ The correct answer is 14/255.

Additional Information

Pythagorean Triplets

These are sets of three integers that strictly satisfy Pythagoras Theorem. Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17).

Trigonometric Identities

The most fundamental identity is sin2 A + cos2 A = 1, from which values of cos A can be directly determined without drawing a triangle.

Tangent Relation

The tangent of an angle can always be derived from sine and cosine using the relation tan A = sin A ÷ cos A.

questions.question: If the diameter of the base of a cone is 56 cm and its curved surface area is 3080 cm 2 , then what will be its volume (in cm 3 )? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: If the diameter of the base of a cone is 56 cm and its curved surface area is 3080 cm<sup>2</sup>, then what will be its volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>)? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius (r) = 56 ÷ 2 = 28 cm.

Slant height (l) = CSA ÷ (πr) = 3080 ÷ (22/7 × 28) = 35 cm.

Using Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5) × 7 → (21, 28, 35), height (h) = √(352 − 282) = 21 cm.

Volume = 1/3 × πr2h = 1/3 × 22/7 × 282 × 21 = 17248 cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 17248 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of the base = 56 cm

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 3080 cm2

Formula Used:

Radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2

CSA = πrl (where l is the slant height)

l2 = r2 + h2

Volume = (1/3)πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ Radius (r) = 56 ÷ 2 = 28 cm

⇒ πrl = 3080

⇒ (22/7) × 28 × l = 3080

⇒ 88 × l = 3080

⇒ l = 3080 ÷ 88 = 35 cm

⇒ h = √(l2 − r2)

⇒ h = √(352 − 282)

⇒ h = √(1225 − 784) = √441 = 21 cm

⇒ Volume = (1/3) × (22/7) × 28 × 28 × 21

⇒ Volume = 22 × 4 × 28 × 7

⇒ Volume = 17248 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 17248 cm3.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of a Cone

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the circular base: TSA = πr(r + l).

Volume of a Cylinder

A cylinder with the same base radius and height as a cone has exactly three times its volume. Volume = πr2h.

Frustum of a Cone

When a cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base, the lower part is a frustum. Volume = (1/3)πh(R2 + r2 + Rr).

questions.question: If A and B are two events such that \(\rm P(A\cup B)=\frac{3}{4}, P(A\cap B) = \frac{1}{4}\) and \(\rm P(B) = \frac{1}2\) , then the events A and B are _____.
questions.questionHtml: If A and B are two events such that \(\rm P(A\cup B)=\frac{3}{4}, P(A\cap B) = \frac{1}{4}\) and \(\rm P(B) = \frac{1}2\) , then the events A and B are _____.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

From the addition theorem: P(A) = P(A ∪ B) + P(A ∩ B) − P(B)

⇒ P(A) = 3/4 + 1/4 − 1/2 = 1/2

Now, calculate P(A) × P(B) = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4

Since P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B) = 1/4, the events A and B are independent.

∴ The correct answer is Independent.

Alternate Method

Given:

P(A ∪ B) = 3/4

P(A ∩ B) = 1/4

P(B) = 1/2

Formula Used:

Addition Rule: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)

Independence Rule: Events are independent if P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B)

Calculation:

⇒ 3/4 = P(A) + 1/2 − 1/4

⇒ 3/4 = P(A) + 1/4

⇒ P(A) = 3/4 − 1/4

⇒ P(A) = 2/4 = 1/2

Now check the condition for independent events:

⇒ P(A) × P(B) = 1/2 × 1/2

⇒ P(A) × P(B) = 1/4

⇒ We are given P(A ∩ B) = 1/4.

⇒ Therefore, P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B)

This perfectly satisfies the condition for independent events.

∴ The correct answer is Independent.

Additional Information

Independent Events

Two events are independent if the occurrence of one does not affect the probability of the other. The key mathematical condition is: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B).

Mutually Exclusive Events

Two events are mutually exclusive if they cannot occur at the same time, meaning they share no common outcomes. The condition is: P(A ∩ B) = 0.

Addition Rule of Probability

For any two overlapping events A and B, the probability of either event occurring is given by the formula: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).

questions.question: Find the median of the following data. Class Interval 0-20 20-40 40-60 60-80 80-100 Frequency 9 16 24 15 4
questions.questionHtml:
Find the median of the following data.

Class Interval 0-20 20-40 40-60 60-80 80-100
Frequency 9 16 24 15 4
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cumulative Frequencies: 9, 25, 49, 64, 68.

Total frequency N = 68 ⇒ N ÷ 2 = 34.

The first cumulative frequency > 34 is 49, hence the median class is 40-60.

Median = l + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Median = 40 + [(34 − 25) ÷ 24] × 20 = 40 + (9 ÷ 24) × 20 = 47.5

∴ The correct answer is 47.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Class Intervals: 0-20, 20-40, 40-60, 60-80, 80-100

Frequencies: 9, 16, 24, 15, 4

Formula Used:

Median = l + [(N/2 − CF) ÷ f] × h

Where:

l = lower limit of median class

N = total frequency

CF = cumulative frequency of the preceding class

f = frequency of the median class

h = class size

Calculations:

⇒ First, let us construct the cumulative frequency (CF) distribution:

⇒ 0-20: 9

⇒ 20-40: 9 + 16 = 25

⇒ 40-60: 25 + 24 = 49

⇒ 60-80: 49 + 15 = 64

⇒ 80-100: 64 + 4 = 68

⇒ Total frequency (N) = 68 ⇒ N ÷ 2 = 68 ÷ 2 = 34

⇒ The cumulative frequency just greater than 34 is 49, corresponding to the class 40-60.

⇒ Median class = 40-60

⇒ Here, l = 40, CF = 25, f = 24, h = 20

⇒ Median = 40 + [(34 − 25) ÷ 24] × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (9 ÷ 24) × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (3 ÷ 8) × 20

⇒ Median = 40 + (60 ÷ 8)

⇒ Median = 40 + 7.5 = 47.5

∴ The correct answer is 47.5.

Additional Information

Mode of Grouped Data

Mode = l + [(f1 − f0) ÷ (2f1 − f0 − f2)] × h, where f1 is the modal class frequency, f0 is the preceding class frequency, and f2 is the succeeding class frequency.

Mean of Grouped Data

Mean = Σ(fixi) ÷ Σfi, where xi represents the class mark or midpoint of each interval, calculated as (lower limit + upper limit) ÷ 2.

Empirical Relationship

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean. This formula is highly useful to find one of the measures of central tendency when the other two are known for a moderately skewed distribution.

questions.question: Two years ago, the population of a town was 9487500. Due to migration to big cities, it decreases every year at the rate of 8%. The present population of the town is:
questions.questionHtml: Two years ago, the population of a town was 9487500. Due to migration to big cities, it decreases every year at the rate of 8%. The present population of the town is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Present population = Initial Population × (Multiplying Factor)2 = 9487500 × 0.92 × 0.92

Instead of full calculation, apply the Digital Sum method to find the correct option.

Digital sum of 9487500 = 9 + 4 + 8 + 7 + 5 = 33 → 6 and 0.92 = 9 + 2 = 11 → 2

Resulting Digital Sum = 6 × 2 × 2 = 24 → 6

Only the value 8030220 has a digital sum of 6 (8 + 0 + 3 + 0 + 2 + 2 + 0 = 15 → 6).

∴ The correct answer is 8030220.

Alternate Method

Given:

Population 2 years ago (P) = 9487500

Rate of decrease (R) = 8% per year

Time (n) = 2 years

Formula Used:

A = P × (1 − R / 100)n

Calculations:

⇒ Present Population (A) = 9487500 × (1 − 8 / 100)2

⇒ A = 9487500 × (92 / 100)2

⇒ A = 9487500 × (23 / 25) × (23 / 25)

⇒ A = 9487500 × (529 / 625)

⇒ A = 15180 × 529

⇒ A = 8030220

∴ The correct answer is 8030220.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Decrease

If a value decreases by x% and y% successively, the net percentage change is given by: Net Decrease = −x − y + (x × y) / 100 %. For a repeated 8% decrease, the overall effective reduction is −8 − 8 + 0.64 = −15.36%.

Digital Sum Concept

The digital sum is found by repeatedly adding the digits of a number until a single digit remains. In multiplication, the Digital Sum of the product equals the product of the Digital Sums of the individual multipliers. It is a highly reliable shortcut for verifying complex decimal and fraction multiplications.

Population Growth & Decay Formula

When a population uniformly changes at R% per year for n years, the new population is directly calculated using the compound interest formula approach: A = P × (1 ± R / 100)n.

questions.question: Adi and Dia together have ₹1,440. If \(\frac{3}{10}\) of Adi's amount is equal to \(\frac{3}{5}\) of Dia's amount, how much amount does Dia have?
questions.questionHtml: Adi and Dia together have ₹1,440. If \(\frac{3}{10}\) of Adi's amount is equal to \(\frac{3}{5}\) of Dia's amount, how much amount does Dia have?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Equating the fractions: (3/10) × Adi = (3/5) × Dia

Ratio of Adi to Dia = (3/5) : (3/10) = 2 : 1

Total parts = 2 + 1 = 3 parts, which corresponds to ₹1440.

Dia's share = 1 part = 1440 ÷ 3 = ₹480.

∴ The correct answer is ₹480.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total amount of Adi and Dia = ₹1440

(3/10) of Adi's amount = (3/5) of Dia's amount

Calculations:

⇒ Let Adi's amount be A and Dia's amount be D.

⇒ (3/10) × A = (3/5) × D

⇒ A / D = (3/5) × (10/3)

⇒ A / D = 30 / 15 = 2 / 1

⇒ This implies A = 2D

⇒ We know that A + D = 1440

⇒ 2D + D = 1440

⇒ 3D = 1440

⇒ D = 1440 ÷ 3 = 480

∴ The correct answer is ₹480.

Additional Information

Ratio & Proportion

When a given quantity is divided into a ratio a : b, the first part is (a / (a + b)) × Total and the second part is (b / (a + b)) × Total.

Equality of Fractions

If fractions multiplied by quantities are equal (e.g., x × A = y × B), their inverse ratio yields the ratio of the quantities (A : B = y : x). This is highly useful for directly converting fractional relations into ratios.

questions.question: The LCM of 2 3 × 9 2 × 13, 2 2 × 13 2 × 19 and 9 3 × 13 2 × 19 2 is
questions.questionHtml: The LCM of 2<sup>3</sup> × 9<sup>2</sup> × 13, 2<sup>2</sup> × 13<sup>2</sup> × 19 and 9<sup>3</sup> × 13<sup>2</sup> × 19<sup>2</sup> is

options.html: 23 × 93 × 132 × 192
23 × 92 × 13 × 19​2
23 × 92 × 132 × 19​3
23 × 92 × 132 × 19​

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To find the LCM of exponential numbers, directly pick the highest power for each distinct base across all given terms.

Bases present in the given expressions: 2, 9, 13, and 19.

Highest power for 2 is 3 → 23

Highest power for 9 is 3 → 93

Highest power for 13 is 2 and for 19 is 2 → 132 × 192

∴ The correct answer is 23 × 93 × 132 × 192.

Alternate Method

Given:

First term = 23 × 92 × 13

Second term = 22 × 132 × 19

Third term = 93 × 132 × 192

Formula Used:

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of expressions is the product of all distinct bases raised to their highest respective powers.

Calculation:

⇒ Let us list the powers of all distinct bases for each given term:

⇒ For base 2: The powers are 3, 2, and 0. The highest power is 3.

⇒ For base 9: The powers are 2, 0, and 3. The highest power is 3.

⇒ For base 13: The powers are 1, 2, and 2. The highest power is 2.

⇒ For base 19: The powers are 0, 1, and 2. The highest power is 2.

⇒ Taking the product of these highest powers, we get the required LCM.

⇒ LCM = 23 × 93 × 132 × 192

∴ The correct answer is 23 × 93 × 132 × 192.

Additional Information

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

To find the HCF of numbers in exponential form, select the lowest power of each common prime factor across all numbers.

Product of Two Numbers

For any two numbers A and B: A × B = LCM(A, B) × HCF(A, B). Note that this rule applies only to exactly two numbers, not three or more.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is simply their product.

questions.question: The age of some students is given in years as 12, 13, 16, 18,14, 19, 13, 17, 15 and 11. The median age (in years) of the students is:
questions.questionHtml: The age of some students is given in years as 12, 13, 16, 18,14, 19, 13, 17, 15 and 11. The median age (in years) of the students is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Arrange the given data in ascending order: 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19.

Since the number of terms n = 10 (even), the median is the simple average of the two middle terms.

Median = Average of the 5th and 6th terms.

Median = (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5.

∴ The correct answer is 14.5 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

The ages of 10 students (in years): 12, 13, 16, 18, 14, 19, 13, 17, 15, and 11.

Formula Used:

For an even number of observations n, Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

Calculation:

⇒ Total number of observations, n = 10 (even number).

⇒ First, sort the given ages in ascending order:

⇒ 11, 12, 13, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19

⇒ Median = [(10/2)th term + (10/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Median = [5th term + 6th term] ÷ 2

⇒ Here, the 5th term is 14, and the 6th term is 15.

⇒ Median = (14 + 15) ÷ 2

⇒ Median = 29 ÷ 2 = 14.5

∴ The correct answer is 14.5 years.

Additional Information

Mean

The mean is the simple average of a given set of numbers. It is calculated by Mean = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations.

Median

The median is the exact middle value when a data set is ordered from least to greatest. If n is odd, Median = ((n+1)÷2)th term. If n is even, the Median is the average of the two central terms.

Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A set of data may have one mode, multiple modes, or no mode at all.

questions.questionHtml:
Akshay places three identical rings of diameter 21 cm in such a manner that each one touches the other two rings. He observes that there is a space enclosed by the circles. What is the area (in cm2) of this portion? (Take π = \(\frac{22}{7}\))

Note — Rounded off to nearest 2 decimal places and √3 = 1.732
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area enclosed by three equal circles touching each other = r2(√3 − π/2) where r = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm.

Enclosed Area = (10.5)2 × (1.732 − 11/7)

Enclosed Area = (110.25 × 1.732) − (110.25 × 11 ÷ 7)

Enclosed Area = 190.953 − 173.25 = 17.703 ≈ 17.70 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 17.70 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of each ring = 21 cm

Radius (r) = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm

Concept Used:

When three identical circles touch each other externally, their centers form an equilateral triangle with side length equal to 2r.

Area of enclosed space = Area of Equilateral Triangle − Area of 3 Sectors enclosed inside the triangle

Calculations:

⇒ Side of the equilateral triangle (a) = r + r = 10.5 + 10.5 = 21 cm

⇒ Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 4) × a2

⇒ Area of equilateral triangle = (1.732 ÷ 4) × 212

⇒ Area of equilateral triangle = 0.433 × 441 = 190.953 cm2

⇒ The equilateral triangle has three interior angles of 60°, so the three sectors combined form a semi-circle (180°).

⇒ Area of the 3 sectors = (1 ÷ 2) × π × r2

⇒ Area of the 3 sectors = (1 ÷ 2) × (22 ÷ 7) × (10.5)2

⇒ Area of the 3 sectors = 11 × 1.5 × 10.5 = 173.25 cm2

⇒ Area of enclosed space = 190.953 − 173.25 = 17.703 cm2

⇒ Rounding off to nearest 2 decimal places, we get 17.70 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 17.70 cm2.

Additional Information

Area of Enclosed Space Between Three Circles

When three equal circles of radius r touch each other externally, the area of the enclosed space is mathematically given as r2(√3 − π/2).

Perimeter of the Enclosed Space

The boundary of the enclosed space is formed by three inward arcs of 60° each. Its total perimeter is equal to the circumference of a semi-circle, which is πr.

Radius of Inscribed Circle

The radius of the largest possible circle that can be inscribed exactly in the empty space between three touching identical circles is r((2 ÷ √3) − 1).

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, an arc ABC subtends an angle of 134° at the centre of the circle. The chord AB is produced to a point P. ∠CBP is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, an arc ABC subtends an angle of 134° at the centre of the circle. The chord AB is produced to a point P. ∠CBP is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The angle subtended by an arc at the major arc is half of the angle subtended at the centre.

⇒ Interior opposite angle = 134° ÷ 2 = 67°.

For any cyclic quadrilateral, the exterior angle is directly equal to the interior opposite angle.

⇒ ∠CBP = Interior opposite angle = 67°.

∴ The correct answer is 67°.

Alternate Method

Given:

∠AOC = 134° (Angle subtended by arc ABC at the centre)

AB is produced to P

Formula Used:

Angle subtended at circumference = Angle at centre ÷ 2

Sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral = 180°

Angles on a straight line add up to 180°

Calculations:

⇒ Let D be a point on the major arc AC. Points A, B, C, and D form a cyclic quadrilateral.

⇒ The angle subtended by arc AC at the centre is ∠AOC = 134°.

⇒ The angle subtended by the same arc at the major arc is ∠ADC.

⇒ ∠ADC = ∠AOC ÷ 2

⇒ ∠ADC = 134° ÷ 2 = 67°

⇒ Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of its opposite angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠ADC = 180°

⇒ ∠ABC + 67° = 180°

⇒ ∠ABC = 180° − 67° = 113°

⇒ Line segment ABP is a straight line, so angles ∠ABC and ∠CBP form a linear pair.

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠CBP = 180°

⇒ 113° + ∠CBP = 180°

⇒ ∠CBP = 180° − 113° = 67°

∴ The correct answer is 67°.

Additional Information

Angle at Centre Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on a circle is called a cyclic quadrilateral. The sum of either pair of opposite angles is exactly 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

If one side of a cyclic quadrilateral is produced, the exterior angle so formed is equal to the interior opposite angle. In this question directly, ∠CBP = ∠ADC = 67°.

questions.question: The ratio between the length and the breadth of a rectangular park is 3 : 2, and the perimeter of the park is 120 m. Find the area (in m 2 ) of the park.
questions.questionHtml: The ratio between the length and the breadth of a rectangular park is 3 : 2, and the perimeter of the park is 120 m. Find the area (in m<sup>2</sup>) of the park.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Sum of length and breadth = Perimeter ÷ 2 = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 m.

Value of 1 ratio part = 60 ÷ (3 + 2) = 60 ÷ 5 = 12.

Length = 3 × 12 = 36 m, Breadth = 2 × 12 = 24 m.

Area = 36 × 24 = 864 m2.

∴ The correct answer is 864 m2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of length (L) and breadth (B) = 3 : 2

Perimeter of the park = 120 m

Formula Used:

Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (L + B)

Area of a rectangle = L × B

Calculation:

Let the length and breadth of the rectangular park be 3x and 2x respectively.

⇒ 2 × (3x + 2x) = 120

⇒ 2 × 5x = 120

⇒ 10x = 120

⇒ x = 12

⇒ Length = 3x = 3 × 12 = 36 m

⇒ Breadth = 2x = 2 × 12 = 24 m

⇒ Area = 36 × 24 = 864 m2

∴ The correct answer is 864 m2.

Additional Information

Properties of a Rectangle

Opposite sides are equal and parallel. Every interior angle is 90°. Length of diagonal = √(L2 + B2).

Square

A special type of rectangle where all four sides are equal. Perimeter = 4a. Area = a2, where 'a' is the side length.

Parallelogram

A quadrilateral with opposite sides parallel. Area = Base × Height. Perimeter = 2(a + b), where 'a' and 'b' are adjacent sides.

E scored more than F but less than C. Marks scored by C were a multiple of 11 and less than 70. The sum of marks scored by C and F was 120. What is the score of F?
questions.solution:
Given: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G scored different marks (out of 100) in an exam.

G scored the lowest marks. B scored second highest marks, which were 80. A scored 72.

So the order, so far, is _ > 80 (B) > 72 (A) > _ > _ >  _ > G.

E scored more than F but less than C. Marks scored by C were a multiple of 11 and less than 70.

The sum of marks scored by C and F was 120. C scored a multiple of 11 and less than 70. The multiples of 11 less than 70 are 11, 22, 33, 44, 55, and 66.

E scored less than C, and the sum of C and F is 120.

Let's test the possible values of C. If C = 66, then F = 120 - 66 = 54. This satisfies the condition that E is between F and C.

C scored 66 and F scored 54.

The current order is  _ > 80 (B) > 72 (A) > 66 (C) > E > 54 (F) > G.

D is the only remaining person.

So the final order is  D > 80 (B) > 72 (A) > 66 (C) > E > 54 (F) > G.

Here, F scored 54.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question: The equation \(\rm F=k\left(q_1\times \frac{q_2}{r^2}\right)\) is representation of: (Where F is the attractive or repulsive electric force of two point charges q 1 and q 2 and r is the distance between two charges)
questions.questionHtml:
The equation \(\rm F=k\left(q_1\times \frac{q_2}{r^2}\right)\) is representation of:  

(Where F is the attractive or repulsive electric force of two point charges q1 and q2 and r is the distance between two charges)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Coulomb's law.

Key Points

  • Coulomb's law states that the electric force (F) between two point charges (q1 and q2) is directly proportional to the product of the magnitudes of charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance (r) between them.
  • The law is mathematically represented as F = k * (q1 * q2) / r², where k is Coulomb's constant.
  • Coulomb's constant (k) is approximately equal to 8.9875 × 10⁹ N m²/C² in vacuum.
  • The force can be attractive or repulsive depending on the nature of the charges (like charges repel, unlike charges attract).

Additional Information

  • Biot-Savart Law:
    • This law relates magnetic fields to the currents which are their sources.
    • It is used to calculate the magnetic field produced by a steady current.
  • Charles's Law:
    • It describes how gases tend to expand when heated.
    • The law states that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature, assuming the pressure is constant.
  • Ohm's Law:
    • It states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
    • It is commonly written as V = IR, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.

Key Points

  • According to the Indian Constitution, the qualifications for appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court are outlined in Article 124.
  • An individual must be a judge of one or more High Courts for at least five years.
  • Alternatively, an individual should have been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years.
  • The person can also be deemed a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President of India.
  • Being an advocate of the Supreme Court for ten years is not a recognized qualification for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.

Additional Information

  • Article 124 of the Indian Constitution
    • It deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court of India.
    • It prescribes the qualifications, appointment, and tenure of the judges of the Supreme Court.
  • Appointment of Judges
    • The President of India appoints the judges of the Supreme Court.
    • The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President after consultation with other judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts as deemed necessary.
  • Tenure of Judges
    • Supreme Court judges hold office until they attain the age of 65 years.
    • They may resign by writing to the President or can be removed by the President on grounds of proven misbehavior or incapacity.
  • Removal of Judges
    • A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed by an order of the President only after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
    • This process is known as 'impeachment'.

questions.question: Which letter code indicates mid-latitude desert climate in Köppen climate classification?
questions.questionHtml: Which letter code indicates mid-latitude desert climate in Köppen climate classification?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is BWk.

Key Points

  • In the Köppen climate classification, BWk represents the mid-latitude desert climate.
  • This climate type is characterized by low annual precipitation, typically less than 250 mm (10 inches).
  • BWk climates usually have hot summers and cold winters, distinguishing them from the hot desert climates (BWh).
  • Examples of regions with BWk climate include parts of the Gobi Desert in Mongolia and China.
  • This classification helps in understanding the geographical distribution of arid and semi-arid regions.

Additional Information

  • Köppen Climate Classification
    • Developed by Vladimir Köppen, this classification system categorizes the world's climates based on temperature and precipitation.
    • The main categories are Tropical (A), Dry (B), Temperate (C), Continental (D), and Polar (E).
    • It is widely used in climatology, geography, and environmental science to study climate patterns.
  • Desert Climate (BWh)
    • Hot desert climates (BWh) have extremely high temperatures during the day and cool temperatures at night.
    • These regions receive very little rainfall, often less than 250 mm annually.
    • Examples include the Sahara Desert in Africa and the Arabian Desert in the Middle East.
  • Steppe Climate (BSk)
    • Steppe climates (BSk) are semi-arid regions that receive slightly more precipitation than deserts.
    • These areas have hot summers and cool to cold winters.
    • Examples include the Great Plains in the United States and the Eurasian Steppe.
  • Climate Change Impact
    • Climate change is altering precipitation patterns, potentially expanding desert and semi-arid areas.
    • Understanding climate classifications helps in predicting and mitigating the impacts of climate change.

questions.question: In which year was the fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson? The model commonly represented cell membrane structure and dynamics.
questions.questionHtml: In which year was the fluid mosaic model proposed by Singer and Nicolson? The model commonly represented cell membrane structure and dynamics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1972.

Key Points

  • The fluid mosaic model was proposed by S.J. Singer and G.L. Nicolson in 1972.
  • This model describes the structure of cell membranes as a mosaic of components that gives the membrane a fluid character.
  • It emphasizes that the cell membrane is flexible and constantly in motion, rather than being static.
  • The model was revolutionary for illustrating the dynamic nature of the lipid bilayer and the embedded proteins.

Additional Information

  • Lipid Bilayer:
    • A double layer of lipids that forms the core structure of the cell membrane.
    • Each lipid molecule has a hydrophilic (water-attracting) head and two hydrophobic (water-repelling) tails.
  • Integral Proteins:
    • Proteins that are embedded within the lipid bilayer.
    • They can span the entire membrane (transmembrane proteins) or be attached to only one side.
  • Peripheral Proteins:
    • Proteins that are attached to the exterior or interior surfaces of the lipid bilayer.
    • They are not embedded within the lipid bilayer.
  • Fluidity:
    • Refers to the viscous nature of the lipid bilayer, allowing lateral movement of molecules within the layer.
    • Fluidity is influenced by temperature and the composition of the lipid molecules.
  • Mosaic Nature:
    • Describes the heterogeneous composition of the cell membrane, including lipids, proteins, and carbohydrates.
    • These components are not uniformly distributed, contributing to the diverse functionality of the cell membrane.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of the International Comparison Programme (ICP), led by the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD)?
questions.questionHtml: What is the primary goal of the International Comparison Programme (ICP), led by the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD)?

options.text: To calculate Purchasing Power Parities (PPPs) and price level indices
options.html: To calculate Purchasing Power Parities (PPPs) and price level indices

options.text: To collect data on international trade
options.html: To collect data on international trade

questions.solution:
The correct answer is To calculate Purchasing Power Parities (PPPs) and price level indices.

Key Points

  • The International Comparison Programme (ICP) is a global statistical initiative led by the United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD).
  • The primary goal of the ICP is to calculate Purchasing Power Parities (PPPs) and price level indices across different countries.
  • PPPs allow for the comparison of the purchasing power of countries' currencies by measuring the relative price levels of a fixed basket of goods and services.
  • These calculations are essential for making more accurate comparisons of economic indicators like GDP and income levels across countries.
  • The ICP data is used by international organizations, policymakers, and researchers to inform economic policies and development strategies.

Additional Information

  • Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)
    • PPP is a method used to determine the relative value of different currencies.
    • It involves comparing the cost of a common basket of goods and services in different countries.
    • PPP helps to eliminate the differences in price levels between countries, providing a more accurate measure of economic performance.
  • Price Level Indices
    • These indices measure the relative cost of living between countries.
    • They are used to compare the average price levels of goods and services in different economies.
    • This helps to identify which countries have higher or lower costs of living relative to others.
  • GDP Comparisons
    • GDP comparisons using PPPs provide a more accurate reflection of the economic output of different countries.
    • They account for differences in price levels, making it possible to compare the real purchasing power of income and expenditure across countries.
  • International Organizations
    • Organizations like the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) use ICP data to analyze global economic trends.
    • This data is crucial for developing global economic policies and for making cross-country comparisons.

questions.question: Which amino acid is a precursor to serotonin, a neurotransmitter that regulates your appetite, sleep and mood?
questions.questionHtml: Which amino acid is a precursor to serotonin, a neurotransmitter that regulates your appetite, sleep and mood?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Tryptophan.

Key Points

  • Tryptophan is an essential amino acid that serves as a precursor for serotonin synthesis in the human body.
  • Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that plays a critical role in regulating mood, appetite, and sleep.
  • Tryptophan is absorbed from dietary sources such as turkey, chicken, milk, cheese, yogurt, eggs, nuts, seeds, tofu, and soy products.
  • Once ingested, tryptophan undergoes hydroxylation and decarboxylation to produce serotonin in the brain.

Additional Information

  • Serotonin
    • Serotonin is also known as 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT).
    • It is primarily found in the gastrointestinal tract, blood platelets, and the central nervous system.
    • In the brain, serotonin is involved in the regulation of mood, anxiety, and happiness.
    • Abnormal levels of serotonin are linked to depression, anxiety disorders, and other mood disorders.
  • Essential Amino Acids
    • Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized by the body and must be obtained from the diet.
    • There are nine essential amino acids, including tryptophan, histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, and valine.
  • Hydroxylation and Decarboxylation
    • Hydroxylation is a chemical process that introduces a hydroxyl group (-OH) into an organic compound.
    • Decarboxylation is a chemical reaction that removes a carboxyl group and releases carbon dioxide (CO2).
  • Dietary Sources of Tryptophan
    • Animal-based sources: Turkey, chicken, milk, cheese, yogurt, and eggs.
    • Plant-based sources: Nuts, seeds, tofu, soy products, and legumes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an antecedent river in India?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is NOT an antecedent river in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Yamuna.

Key Points

  • The Yamuna river is not an antecedent river in India. It is a tributary of the Ganga river.
  • Antecedent rivers are those that maintain their original course and pattern despite the changes in the underlying rock topography.
  • The Ganga, Kosi, and Indus rivers are examples of antecedent rivers in India.
  • Yamuna river originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Himalayas and flows through the states of Uttarakhand, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh before merging with the Ganga at Prayagraj.

Additional Information

  • Antecedent Rivers
    • These are rivers that were established before the current topography was formed.
    • They have the ability to cut through rising mountain ranges due to their strong erosive power.
    • Examples include the Indus, Ganga, and Kosi rivers.
  • Yamuna River
    • It is the largest tributary river of the Ganga in northern India.
    • The river has significant cultural and religious importance in India.
    • Major cities along the Yamuna include Delhi, Mathura, and Agra.
  • Ganga River
    • The Ganga is one of the major rivers in India and holds immense religious significance.
    • It is an antecedent river, originating from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas.
    • It flows through northern India into Bangladesh, eventually emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
  • Indus River
    • The Indus is a major transboundary river in Asia, flowing through China, India, and Pakistan.
    • It is also an antecedent river, originating in Tibet and flowing through the Himalayas.
    • The Indus River basin is one of the largest in the world, supporting a significant population.

questions.question: Which substance is commonly used as an acid-base indicator, which turns red in acidic solutions and blue in basic solutions?
questions.questionHtml: Which substance is commonly used as an acid-base indicator, which turns red in acidic solutions and blue in basic solutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Litmus paper.

Key Points

  • Litmus paper is a common acid-base indicator used in laboratories.
  • It turns red in acidic solutions (pH less than 7).
  • It turns blue in basic solutions (pH greater than 7).
  • Litmus paper is derived from lichens, which are symbiotic associations between fungi and algae.

Additional Information

  • Acid-Base Indicators
    • Substances that change color based on the pH level of the solution they are in.
    • Common indicators include methyl orange, phenolphthalein, and bromothymol blue.
    • Each indicator has a specific pH range over which it changes color.
  • pH Scale
    • A scale ranging from 0 to 14 used to measure how acidic or basic a solution is.
    • A pH of 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic, and above 7 is basic.
  • Lichens
    • Organisms formed from a symbiotic relationship between fungi and algae.
    • They are capable of surviving in harsh environments and are used to produce litmus.
  • Uses of Litmus Paper
    • Commonly used in educational laboratories to teach about acids and bases.
    • Used for testing the acidity or alkalinity of various substances in industrial applications.

questions.question: In which of the following years did Mahatma Gandhi led the Satyagraha and hunger strike for the first time in India?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following years did Mahatma Gandhi led the Satyagraha and hunger strike for the first time in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1918.

Key Points

  • Mahatma Gandhi led the first Satyagraha and hunger strike in India in 1918.
  • This event is known as the Ahmedabad mill workers.
  • The Satyagraha was aimed at addressing the grievances of farmers who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions.
  • Gandhi's leadership in this non-violent protest marked the beginning of his prominent role in the Indian independence movement.
  • The success of the Ahmedabad mill workers established the effectiveness of non-violent resistance in India.

Additional Information

  • Champaran Satyagraha:
    • This was Gandhi's first active involvement in the Indian independence movement.
    • It was a major success and demonstrated the power of non-violent resistance (Satyagraha).
    • Gandhi arrived in Champaran in 1917 and led the movement in 1918.
    • It resulted in the abolition of the oppressive tinkathia system where farmers were forced to grow indigo on a portion of their land.
  • Satyagraha:
    • A form of non-violent resistance or civil resistance.
    • The term was coined and developed by Mahatma Gandhi.
    • It played a significant role in the Indian independence movement and influenced numerous other freedom and civil rights movements globally.
  • Indigo Cultivation:
    • Indigo was a cash crop grown in India during British rule.
    • Farmers were often forced to grow indigo by British planters under oppressive conditions.
    • The Champaran Satyagraha specifically addressed the exploitation and hardships faced by indigo farmers.
  • Non-violent Resistance:
    • A method of protest that seeks to achieve goals through symbolic protests, civil disobedience, and other non-violent means.
    • Gandhi's philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) was central to his approach to resistance.
    • Non-violent resistance has been adopted by various movements around the world, including the Civil Rights Movement in the United States.

questions.question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme court of India give a ruling that, 'in case of any conflict between the fundamental rights and the directive principles, the former would prevail'?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following cases did the Supreme court of India give a ruling that, 'in case of any conflict between the fundamental rights and the directive principles, the former would prevail'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Champakam Dorairajan Case, 1951.

Key Points

  • The Supreme Court of India ruled in the Champakam Dorairajan Case, 1951, that fundamental rights have supremacy over directive principles in case of any conflict between the two.
  • This landmark judgment emphasized the importance of fundamental rights as enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
  • The case involved the challenge against a communal Government Order of Madras that provided caste-based reservations in educational institutions.
  • The Supreme Court held that such reservations violated the fundamental right to equality guaranteed under Article 15(1).
  • Consequently, this ruling led to the First Amendment of the Constitution in 1951, allowing the state to make special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes.

Additional Information

  • Fundamental Rights
    • Fundamental Rights are the basic human rights guaranteed to all citizens by the Constitution of India.

questions.question: When did James Chadwick prove the existence of the neutron – an elementary particle devoid of any electric charge?
questions.questionHtml: When did James Chadwick prove the existence of the neutron – an elementary particle devoid of any electric charge?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1932.

Key Points

  • James Chadwick, an English physicist, proved the existence of the neutron in 1932.
  • His discovery of the neutron was a significant breakthrough in nuclear physics.
  • Chadwick's experiment involved bombarding beryllium with alpha particles, which resulted in the emission of a new type of radiation.
  • This new radiation was later identified as being composed of neutrons, particles with no electric charge.
  • Chadwick was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935 for his discovery of the neutron.

Additional Information

  • Neutron:
    • A neutron is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of an atom.
    • It has no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than that of a proton.
    • Neutrons play a crucial role in the stability of atomic nuclei.
  • Alpha particles:
    • Alpha particles are a type of ionizing radiation ejected by certain radioactive materials.
    • They consist of two protons and two neutrons bound together.
    • Alpha particles are relatively heavy and positively charged.
  • Nobel Prize in Physics:
    • It is one of the most prestigious awards in the field of physics.
    • James Chadwick received this honor in 1935 for his discovery of the neutron.
    • The Nobel Prize in Physics recognizes outstanding contributions to the field of physics.
  • Nuclear Physics:
    • It is a branch of physics that studies the constituents and interactions of atomic nuclei.
    • The discovery of the neutron was a major milestone in nuclear physics.
    • Nuclear physics has applications in various fields, including energy production and medical imaging.

questions.question: Who discovered the laws of levers and pulleys, which allow us to move heavy objects using small forces?
questions.questionHtml: Who discovered the laws of levers and pulleys, which allow us to move heavy objects using small forces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Archimedes.

Key Points

  • Archimedes was a Greek mathematician, physicist, engineer, inventor, and astronomer.
  • He is known for formulating the law of the lever, which states that the force needed to move an object is inversely proportional to the distance from the pivot point.
  • Archimedes also discovered the principle of mechanical advantage in the use of pulleys.
  • His work laid the foundation for the field of statics, which studies forces in static equilibrium.
  • Archimedes’ contributions greatly influenced the development of both theoretical and applied mechanics.

Additional Information

  • Levers:
    • A lever is a simple machine consisting of a rigid beam and a fulcrum, used to magnify force.
    • The three classes of levers are determined by the relative positions of the load, effort, and fulcrum.
    • Levers are used in various applications, from seesaws to crowbars and scissors.
  • Pulleys:
    • A pulley is a wheel on an axle or shaft designed to support the movement and change the direction of a taut cable.
    • Pulleys are used to lift loads, apply forces, and transmit power.
    • They can be combined to form a block and tackle, which significantly reduces the amount of force needed to lift a load.
  • Statics:
    • Statics is the branch of mechanics that deals with bodies at rest and forces in equilibrium.
    • It involves analyzing the distribution of forces and their impact on structures.
    • Statics principles are essential for the design and analysis of buildings, bridges, and other structures.
  • Archimedean Principle:
    • The Archimedean principle states that a body submerged in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the body.
    • This principle explains why objects float or sink in water.
    • It is a fundamental concept in fluid mechanics and engineering.

questions.question: The productivity of which of the following crops had initially increased due to the Green Revolution?
questions.questionHtml: The productivity of which of the following crops had initially increased due to the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Wheat and rice.

Key Points

  • The Green Revolution in India began in the 1960s and was primarily aimed at increasing agricultural productivity.
  • Wheat and rice were the primary beneficiaries of the Green Revolution due to the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds.
  • The use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and improved irrigation techniques further boosted the productivity of these crops.
  • The Green Revolution led to self-sufficiency in food grains, particularly in wheat and rice, significantly reducing India's dependence on food imports.
  • Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh were the major regions where the impact of the Green Revolution on wheat and rice production was most significant.

Additional Information

  • High-Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:
    • HYV seeds were a cornerstone of the Green Revolution, designed to produce more grain per plant.
    • These seeds required proper irrigation, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides to achieve high yields.
  • Fertilizers and Pesticides:
    • The Green Revolution saw a massive increase in the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides to enhance crop productivity.
    • While these inputs increased yields, they also led to environmental concerns and soil degradation over time.
  • Irrigation:
    • Improved irrigation facilities, including the construction of dams and canal systems, were crucial for the success of the Green Revolution.
    • Reliable water supply was essential for the HYV seeds to reach their full potential.
  • Socio-Economic Impact:
    • The Green Revolution led to increased agricultural income and improved living standards for many farmers in the areas where it was implemented.
    • However, it also widened the income disparity between large and small farmers, as the latter often could not afford the necessary inputs.
  • Long-Term Challenges:
    • The intensive farming practices led to issues such as groundwater depletion, soil health deterioration, and increased pest resistance.
    • There is a need for sustainable agricultural practices to address these long-term challenges.

questions.question: ROM is primarily used for which of the following purposes?
questions.questionHtml: ROM is primarily used for which of the following purposes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Storing the BIOS or firmware.

Key Points

  • ROM (Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile memory, which means it retains its data even when the power is turned off.
  • It is primarily used to store the BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) or firmware of a computer, which is essential for the initial boot process.
  • The BIOS or firmware contains the necessary instructions for the computer to start up and communicate with its hardware components.
  • ROM is not meant for random data access or temporary data storage, as it can only be read and not easily modified.

Additional Information

  • BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)
    • It is the firmware used to perform hardware initialization during the booting process.
    • BIOS provides runtime services for operating systems and programs.
    • The BIOS firmware is built into the PC and is the first software that runs when powered on.
  • Firmware
    • Firmware is a specific class of computer software that provides low-level control for a device's specific hardware.
    • It is embedded in the hardware and can be updated to improve functionality and security.
  • EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory)
    • A type of ROM that can be electronically erased and reprogrammed.
    • It allows for limited write cycles, making it useful for storing configuration settings.
  • Volatile vs. Non-Volatile Memory
    • Volatile memory requires power to maintain stored information (e.g., RAM).
    • Non-volatile memory retains data even when the power is turned off (e.g., ROM, Flash Memory).

questions.question: The _________ method is commonly used to verify the integrity of data.
questions.questionHtml: The _________ method is commonly used to verify the integrity of data.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Hashing.

Key Points

  • Hashing is a process of converting data into a fixed-size string of characters, which is typically a hash code.
  • It is commonly used to verify the integrity of data by ensuring that the data has not been altered.
  • Hash functions are designed to be fast and to produce unique hashes for unique inputs.
  • Popular hashing algorithms include MD5, SHA-1, and SHA-256, each with varying levels of security.
  • Hashing is widely used in applications such as password storage, data verification, and digital signatures.

Additional Information

  • Hash Function
    • A hash function takes an input and returns a fixed-size string of bytes.
    • Even a small change to the input will produce a significantly different output.
  • Collision
    • A collision occurs when two different inputs produce the same hash output.
    • Good hash functions minimize the chances of collisions.
  • MD5
    • MD5 (Message Digest Algorithm 5) produces a 128-bit hash value.
    • It is widely used but is considered cryptographically broken and unsuitable for further use.
  • SHA-256
    • SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit) is part of the SHA-2 family, designed by the NSA.
    • It produces a 256-bit hash value and is widely used in security applications and protocols.
  • Digital Signatures
    • Hashing is used in digital signatures to create a unique representation of data.
    • Digital signatures ensure data authenticity and integrity.

questions.question: What type of media is commonly used for WAN communication?
questions.questionHtml: What type of media is commonly used for WAN communication?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Fiber Optic Cable.

Key Points

  • Fiber optic cables use light to transmit data, allowing for high-speed data transfer over long distances.
  • They are less susceptible to electromagnetic interference, making them ideal for WAN communication where signal integrity is crucial.
  • Fiber optic cables can carry significantly more data compared to traditional copper cables, supporting higher bandwidths.
  • Due to their efficiency and reliability, fiber optic cables are widely used in modern WANs, including internet backbones and global telecommunications networks.
  • They are essential for applications requiring high data transmission rates, such as video conferencing, online gaming, and cloud computing.

Additional Information

  • HDMI Cable
    • HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) cables are used primarily for transmitting audio and video signals between devices like TVs, monitors, and gaming consoles.
    • They are not suitable for WAN communication due to their limited range and use case.
  • Twisted Pair Cable
    • Twisted pair cables are commonly used for LAN (Local Area Network) connections, such as in Ethernet networks.
    • While they can be used for shorter WAN links, they are not ideal for long-distance WAN communication.
  • Coaxial Cable
    • Coaxial cables are used for cable television and internet services but are less common for modern WANs due to their lower bandwidth capacity compared to fiber optics.
    • They are more susceptible to signal degradation over long distances.
  • Advantages of Fiber Optic Cables
    • Fiber optic cables offer higher bandwidth, allowing for faster internet speeds and larger data transfers.
    • They have a lower signal attenuation rate, meaning signals can travel longer distances without losing strength.
    • They provide better security as they are harder to tap into without being detected.
    • Fiber optics are lightweight and thinner compared to copper cables, making them easier to install and manage.

questions.question: In a Local Area Network (LAN), which of the following is most commonly used to ensure that data packets are efficiently forwarded to the correct device, based on its MAC address?
questions.questionHtml: In a Local Area Network (LAN), which of the following is most commonly used to ensure that data packets are efficiently forwarded to the correct device, based on its MAC address?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Layer 3 Switch.

Key Points

  • A Layer 3 Switch is designed to function both as a switch and a router, which allows it to efficiently forward data packets to the correct device within a LAN.
  • These switches use MAC addresses to switch data and IP addresses to route data, making them highly efficient in data forwarding.
  • Layer 3 switches are commonly used in enterprise networks to ensure high performance and low latency in data communication.
  • They are capable of performing routing functions while maintaining the speed and performance of switching.

Additional Information

  • MAC Address (Media Access Control Address)
    • A unique identifier assigned to network interfaces for communications at the data link layer of a network segment.
    • Used in networking technologies such as Ethernet and Wi-Fi.
  • Router
    • A networking device that forwards data packets between computer networks.
    • Routers perform traffic directing functions on the Internet.
  • Hub
    • A basic networking device that connects multiple computers in a LAN.
    • Hubs broadcast data to all devices on a network, which can lead to inefficiencies.
  • Bridge
    • A device that connects and filters traffic between two or more network segments.
    • Operates at the data link layer and helps to reduce network traffic by dividing it into segments.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Central Processing Unit (CPU) is/are correct? The CPU is often referred to as the 'brain' of the computer. The CPU consists of three main units: the control unit (CU), arithmetic logic unit (ALU), and cache memory.
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements about the Central Processing Unit (CPU) is/are correct?

The CPU is often referred to as the 'brain' of the computer.

The CPU consists of three main units: the control unit (CU), arithmetic logic unit (ALU), and cache memory.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

Key Points

  • The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is frequently referred to as the 'brain' of the computer.
  • The CPU is responsible for executing instructions from computer programs by performing basic arithmetic, logical, control, and input/output operations.
  • The CPU typically consists of the Control Unit (CU), the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), and various registers.
  • The Control Unit directs the operation of the processor by fetching and interpreting instructions from memory.

Additional Information

  • Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
    • The ALU is a fundamental part of the CPU that performs arithmetic and logical operations.
    • It operates on binary data inputs and produces binary results, which are stored in registers.
  • Control Unit (CU)
    • The CU directs the operation of the processor by fetching instructions from memory and decoding them.
    • It coordinates the activities of the ALU, registers, and other components.
  • Registers
    • Registers are small, fast storage locations within the CPU used to hold data temporarily.
    • They include the instruction register, program counter, and accumulator, among others.
  • Cache Memory
    • Although not considered one of the three main units of the CPU, cache memory is crucial for improving processing speed.
    • It stores frequently accessed data and instructions to reduce the time taken to fetch them from main memory.

questions.question: What is the size of each ASCII character in bits?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 8 bits.

Key Points

  • Each ASCII character is represented using 8 bits (1 byte).
  • ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.
  • ASCII codes are used to represent text in computers and other devices that use text.
  • The standard ASCII character set includes 128 characters (0 to 127).
  • Extended ASCII sets use the full 8 bits, allowing for 256 characters (0 to 255).

Additional Information

  • Character Encoding
    • Character encoding is a system of converting characters into bytes for storage and transmission.
    • Other popular encoding standards include Unicode, UTF-8, and ISO-8859-1.
  • ASCII History
    • ASCII was developed in the early 1960s by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI).
    • It was designed to standardize character representation across various devices and platforms.
  • ASCII Applications
    • ASCII is widely used in programming, data processing, and communications.
    • It is the basis for text representation in most modern computer systems.
  • Limitations of ASCII
    • Standard ASCII can only represent English characters and a limited set of symbols.
    • Extended ASCII and other encoding schemes were developed to support additional characters and languages.

questions.question: What is a common sign that a computer might be infected with a virus?

Key Points

  • One of the common symptoms of a computer virus infection is unusual system slowdowns that occur without any apparent reason.
  • Unexpected errors and crashes are also indicative of a potential virus infection, disrupting normal operations.
  • Infected systems may display frequent and unwanted pop-up ads, even when not browsing the internet.
  • Another sign is the presence of unknown programs or processes running in the background, which were not installed by the user.
  • Changes in system settings and the appearance of unfamiliar toolbars in the browser can also indicate a virus infection.

Additional Information

  • Virus Definition
    • A computer virus is a type of malicious software program designed to replicate itself by modifying other programs and inserting its own code.
    • Viruses typically require a host program to function and spread from one computer to another.
  • Common Types of Viruses
    • File Infector Virus: Attaches itself to executable files and spreads when the infected file is run.
    • Macro Virus: Embeds itself into documents and spreadsheets that contain macros.
    • Boot Sector Virus: Infects the master boot record and is activated when the computer is started.
  • Prevention Measures
    • Install and regularly update antivirus software to detect and remove viruses.
    • Avoid downloading and opening email attachments from unknown or untrusted sources.
    • Keep your operating system and all software up to date with the latest security patches.
  • Impact of Viruses
    • Viruses can lead to data loss, system corruption, and unauthorized access to sensitive information.
    • They can also cause significant downtime and financial losses for both individuals and organizations.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is It marks the start and end of each part in a multipart message..

Key Points

  • The boundary parameter in the Content-Type header is crucial for distinguishing different parts of a multipart email message.
  • It is an identifier that marks the beginning and ending of each part within the message.
  • Each boundary is a unique string that should not appear in the content of the message parts.
  • The boundary string allows email clients to correctly parse and separate the individual parts of the email, such as text, images, and attachments.

Additional Information

  • Multipart Email:
    • A multipart email contains multiple parts, such as plain text, HTML, and attachments.
    • These parts are separated by boundary strings defined in the Content-Type header.
  • Content-Type Header:
    • It specifies the media type of the resource, for example, text/html for HTML files.
    • In emails, it indicates the type of content, such as multipart/mixed for emails with attachments.
  • MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions):
    • MIME is an Internet standard that extends the format of email to support text in character sets other than ASCII, as well as attachments.
    • It is used to encode the body of the email in a way that can be interpreted by different email clients.
  • Boundary String:
    • A boundary string is a sequence of characters that indicate where parts of the multipart message begin and end.
    • It is defined in the Content-Type header and used by email clients to split the email into its constituent parts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is To prompt for permission before making system-wide changes.

Key Points

  • User Account Control (UAC) is a security feature in Windows operating systems.
  • Its primary role is to prevent unauthorized changes to the operating system.
  • UAC prompts users for permission or an administrator password before allowing changes that could affect the system's operation.
  • It helps in preventing malware and unauthorized applications from making system-wide changes without user consent.
  • UAC adds an additional layer of security by ensuring that all changes to the system settings are intentional.

Additional Information

  • Operating System Security:
    • Operating system security includes measures to protect the OS from threats, including malware and unauthorized access.
    • Common security features include firewalls, antivirus programs, and user account management.
  • Administrator Account:
    • An administrator account has full access to the system and can make system-wide changes.
    • It is recommended to use a standard user account for daily activities and an administrator account only when necessary.
  • Standard User Account:
    • A standard user account has limited access and cannot make system-wide changes without permission.
    • This account is suitable for most daily tasks and helps in maintaining system security.
  • Security Tokens:
    • In UAC, security tokens are used to determine the level of access a user has.
    • When a user logs in, Windows assigns a security token that includes their user rights and privileges.
